name: LML/USDT staking protocol
rootCause: LML/USDT staking protocol on BNB Chain suffered a price manipulation attack. The hacker used flash loans to massively inflate the LML/USDT pool spot price, exploited a logic flaw in the staking contract’s reward calculation (which relied on a stale stored price with a 3600-second cooldown instead of live AMM price), batch-claimed oversized LML rewards from pre-staked addresses via EIP-7702, and sold them in the distorted pool for approximately $950,000 profit, causing the LML token price to crash 99.6%.

descriptions.text: LML/USDT staking protocol on BNB Chain suffered a price manipulation attack. The hacker used flash loans to massively inflate the LML/USDT pool spot price, exploited a logic flaw in the staking contract’s reward calculation (which relied on a stale stored price with a 3600-second cooldown instead of live AMM price), batch-claimed oversized LML rewards from pre-staked addresses via EIP-7702, and sold them in the distorted pool for approximately $950,000 profit, causing the LML token price to crash 99.6%.

On March 31, 2026, the LML/USDT staking protocol on BNB Chain was exploited for approximately $950,000. The attacker manipulated the LML/USDT price via flash-loan-driven trading, then immediately claimed and dumped inflated staking rewards. The exploit stemmed from a reward-claim path that settled using a same-block, attacker-controlled spot price. The APower reward-claim entrypoint allowed rewards to be calculated and settled using a manipulable spot price fetched directly from the LML/USDT AMM. The attacker distorted the price in the same transaction as the reward claim, enabling over-withdrawal.
